title: Affine space and étale localization
statement:
Let $k$ be the standing field, a finite or algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$ and a finite discrete commutative ring $\Lambda$ with $\ell^r\Lambda=0$ for some $r\geq1$. Let $S$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, use ordinary constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves and their unbounded derived category on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $D_{\mathrm{class}}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ be its full subcategory of complexes with classical cohomology sheaves [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]. Via the comparison $\nu_T$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], use the finite etale Tate sheaf $\Lambda_T(1)=\mu_{\ell^r,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}\Lambda_T$, its nonnegative tensor powers, and $K(d)=K\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda_T(d)$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist, def-kun-derived-tensor]. Here these sheaves and twists on the pro-etale site are the exact inverse images of the displayed etale sheaves. For a separated finite-type $f:X\to S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $Rf_!$ on the classical categories is the restriction of $R\bar f_*Dj_!$ for a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\bar X\xrightarrow{\bar f}S$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-weil-extension-by-zero]; $f^!$ denotes its right adjoint on these classical categories.

1. For $d\in\mathbb N$ and the affine-space projection $a:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ [def-sbc-affine-space], this right adjoint exists and is canonically $a^*(-)(d)[2d]$. The unit and counit of this adjunction commute with every change of base $v:S'\to S$ between finite-type $k$-schemes, under the canonical compact-support exchange and the pullback-of-twist identifications.
2. For every separated finite-type $f:X\to S$ this classical right adjoint exists. If $u:U\to X$ is separated, etale and of finite type [def-weil-etale-morphism], then there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$u^*f^!N\xrightarrow{\sim}(fu)^!N\quad\text{in }D_{\mathrm{class}}(U_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)\qquad\text{(G10)}$$
for every $N\in D_{\mathrm{class}}(S_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. Here $Du_!$ is the transport to the classical categories of termwise etale sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. It identifies the composite adjunction $Rf_!Du_!\dashv u^*f^!$ with $R(fu)_!\dashv(fu)^!$; thus it respects units and counits, composition of compact supports, and further separated finite-type etale localization. No adjunction on the whole pro-etale derived categories is asserted.

proof.text: First note the elementary geometric closure checks. A composite of finite-type maps is finite type: over finite affine covers combine the two finite lists of algebra generators, since if $B=A[b_1,\ldots,b_m]$ and $C=B[c_1,\ldots,c_n]$, then $C=A[b_1,\ldots,b_m,c_1,\ldots,c_n]$. For separatedness of $fu$, factor its diagonal as $U\to U\times_XU\to U\times_SU$: the first is the closed diagonal of $u$, and the second is a base change of the closed diagonal of $f$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; the composite is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]. This applies also to the further maps. The compactification $\bar X$ is finite type over $k$ because $S$ is finite type over $k$ and $\bar X\to S$ is finite type; no separatedness of $S$ over $k$ is needed. Every scheme occurring, including $X$, $U$, the $X_i$, and the compactifications, is finite type over $k$ by the finite-type composition calculation above. They are Noetherian: the only ideals of the field $k$ are $0$ and $k$, so $k$ is Noetherian and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies to their finite-type structure maps. They are quasi-compact by the definition of Noetherian, and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Every separated finite-type map under consideration has a compactification by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Put $X_i=\mathbf A^i_S$ and let $a_i:X_i\to X_{i-1}$ forget the last coordinate. On $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ the polynomial-ring equality $R[x_1,\ldots,x_i]=R[x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1}][x_i]$ identifies $a_i$ with the affine line over $X_{i-1}$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Polynomial generators give finite type, and the diagonal is the closed subscheme defined by differences of the two sets of coordinates, giving separatedness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. For any such base $T$ the standard chart $j:\mathbf A^1_T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_T$ and proper projection $q:\mathbf P^1_T\to T$ are a compactification [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion, lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. The integer $\ell^r$ is invertible on every $k$-scheme here and kills $\Lambda$, and $k$ is finite or algebraically closed with $\ell$ invertible in $k$, as the comparison statements of Step 2 require. Thus all coefficient, Noetherian and compactification hypotheses used below hold.

Write $E_T=

u_{T,*}K	o K$ is an isomorphism for every classical $K$. With unit and counit invertible, $E_T$ is an equivalence from the entire ordinary etale derived category onto the entire classical pro-etale category, with quasi-inverse $E_T^{-1}=R
u_{T,*}$. The square comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] intertwines inverse images. The current statement of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] gives this inverse-image square on all unbounded complexes, compatibly with composition, because all four inverse-image functors are exact; its direct-image assertion is only bounded below. The unbounded direct-image comparison used here is [lem-sfb-unbounded-direct-image-comparison]: for every finite-type $g$ between finite-type $k$-schemes, the mate $
u^*Rg_{\mathrm{et},*}K	o Rg_{\mathrm{proet},*}
u^*K$ of that inverse-image square is an isomorphism for every unbounded $K$; the field, finite-type and finite-coefficient hypotheses were verified in Step 1. Composing $g$ pastes the inverse-image squares along the composite inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions, so by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (2) the comparison for a composite is the pasted composite of the two comparisons, and by (4) the comparison for an identity is the identity. For an open $j$, pro-etale extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact], and [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] intertwines the two exact extensions by zero, again termwise. Consequently for any compactification $c=(j, ar f)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$E_SRf_{!,\mathrm{et}}^c\cong E_SR ar f_{\mathrm{et},*}Dj_{!,\mathrm{et}}\cong R ar f_{\mathrm{proet},*}Dj_{!,\mathrm{proet}}E_X.$$
The ordinary candidate is [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Conjugate each unbounded refinement, composition and base-change isomorphism of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] by the equivalences $E$: explicitly replace $F$ by $E_{m target}FE_{m source}^{-1}$ and $t:F	o G$ by $E_{m target}tE_{m source}^{-1}$, inserting the equivalence counits between composite functors. Functoriality preserves $t_2\circ t_1$; the equivalence triangle identities cancel inserted units/counits. Hence each stated identity and associativity diagram commutes after this conjugation. Their maps are the canonical ones: the direct-image comparisons are mates of the inverse-image square, and the open comparison is the adjunction comparison; pasting these squares commutes with taking mates by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Thus their identity, associativity and base-change equations remain equations after applying $E$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: classical comparison, expanded to the actual whole unbounded categories

proof.text:
Let $G_f$ be an ordinary-etale compact-support right adjoint given by [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Define on classical objects $f^!=E_XG_fE_S^{-1}$. For etale $M,L$ the equivalences and Step 2 give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!E_XM,E_SL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,\mathrm{et}}M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,G_fL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E_XM,E_XG_fL).$$
Every classical object has this form, so this proves the adjunction on exactly the stated categories. The canonical comparison of two choices is the unique counit-preserving comparison of right adjoints [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. It is an isomorphism, and its uniqueness makes comparison transitive. Hence the notation $f^!$ is independent of choices in this sense.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph and (2): existence and normalization of the classical right adjoints

proof.text:
It suffices now to compute on the ordinary etale categories. For $a=qj:\mathbf A^1_T\to T$, [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and Step 2 identify $Ra_!$ with $Rq_*Dj_!$. The first assertion of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], applied to the open immersion $j$, which is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], gives $Dj_!\dashv j^*$. Fix the source trace convention first: for $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$, [det-sp-p1-trace] (1)--(2) says that the twisted unit/Kummer-class decomposition has trace equal to projection onto its Kummer-class summand, with value $1$ on that class. Under the exact comparison of Step 2 the unit and the defining Kummer connecting class are their inverse images, so this convention also specifies the ordinary etale trace. In the cyclic case $A=R$, the decomposition $b_q$ and trace $t_q=\operatorname{pr}_2b_q^{-1}$ in [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] have precisely these two component maps and this projection. For arbitrary $A=\Lambda$, that theorem explicitly uses the scalar-extended Kummer class and the same projection definition. Apply it with $N=\ell^r$ to obtain $Rq_*\dashv q^*(-)(1)[2]$, including its specified base-change-compatible trace counit. The composite-adjunction formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_!M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Dj_!M,q^*L(1)[2])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,j^*q^*L(1)[2])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,a^*L(1)[2]).$$
The final identification uses the pullback of the twist [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] and the module-linear composition of inverse images [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], applied termwise using [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. If $H=q^*(-)(1)[2]$, this adjunction has unit $\eta^j$ followed by $j^*\eta^q Dj_!$, and counit $Rq_*\epsilon^j H$ followed by $\epsilon^q$. These are actual composites of the two units and counits, not an arbitrary choice of an adjunction on isomorphic functors.

source.place: Proof (1), d=1: open adjunction composed with the projective-line adjunction

proof.text: The finite Tate factors are flat by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. Thus tensoring with them computes their derived tensor on any complex: the exact tensor functor preserves kernels and images, hence preserves quasi-isomorphisms. By their tensor-power definition [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], reassociation sends $((x\otimes(l_1\otimes\cdots\otimes l_i))\otimes l)$ to $x\otimes(l_1\otimes\cdots\otimes l_i\otimes l)$, with inverse regrouping. It gives $(K(i)[2i])(1)[2]\cong K(i+1)[2i+2]$. The shifts are even, so both differential signs are unchanged; for $i=0$ use the scalar unit map. Pullback commutes with these identifications by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. For the site comparison itself, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies the tensor powers and derived twists with their pro-etale inverse images. Hence the same twist calculation is valid on the classical categories.

source.place: Proof (1), addition of twists and shifts in the affine-space induction

proof.text:
Induct on $i$ for the projection $p_i:X_i\to S$, using the claim $Rp_{i!}\dashv p_i^*(-)(i)[2i]$. At $i=0$, $X_0=S$ by [def-sbc-affine-space]; the identity compactification gives the identity functor by [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and the identity adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] starts the induction. Suppose the claim holds for $i$. Step 4 over the base $X_i$ gives $Ra_{i+1,!}\dashv a_{i+1}^*(-)(1)[2]$. The composition isomorphism [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] and the Hom bijections for the composite adjunction give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_{i+1,!}M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{i+1,!}M,p_i^*L(i)[2i])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,a_{i+1}^*(p_i^*L(i)[2i])(1)[2]).$$
By Step 5 and inverse-image composition [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], the last object is $p_{i+1}^*L(i+1)[2i+2]$. This proves the induction for all $d$. Transporting along Step 2 and using the uniqueness in [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] identifies this computed right adjoint with the chosen $a^!$.

source.place: Proof (1), d=0 and general d via successive affine-line projections

proof.text:
For base change of the affine-line computation, the projective-line adjunction of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] commutes with proper exchange. For the open adjunction, write $b:T'\to T$, $b_U:U'\to U$ and $j':U'\hookrightarrow T'$ for a base change of $j$. The inverse open exchange $\beta:Dj'_!b_U^*\to b^*Dj_!$ is the map of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map], an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], also on complexes by degreewise exactness. Identify $j'^*b^*=b_U^*j^*$. For the unit equation, use the sum-extension presheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] and the sheafified inverse-image construction [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Locally a section of $b_U^*M$ is represented by a section $m$ of $M$ on an etale object over $U$. The unit of sum extension sends $m$ to the summand indexed by that object's lift to $U$. The canonical exchange in the cited formula restricts this section to the fibre product; its transposed map $\beta$ therefore sends the pulled-back lift summand to the same summand in $b^*j_!M$. Restriction by $j'^*$ identifies that summand with the pulled-back section of $M$. Both composites below consequently send every such local generator to the same pulled-back section; additivity and sheafification give the equation:
$$j'^*\beta_M\circ\eta^{j'}_{b_U^*M}=b_U^*\eta^j_M.$$
This is the unit equation. For $K$ on $T$, the counit equation is
$$b^*\epsilon^j_K\circ\beta_{j^*K}=\epsilon^{j'}_{b^*K}.$$
The transpose of the left side under $Dj'_!\dashv j'^*$ is, using the unit equation,
$$b_U^*(j^*\epsilon^j_K\circ\eta^j_{j^*K})=1_{b_U^*j^*K}.$$
The transpose of the right side is the same identity by the triangle identity for $j'$. Injectivity of transposition proves the counit equation. These equations hold in each degree, so they descend to unbounded complexes. The forward open exchange is $\beta^{-1}$ and agrees with [sbc-prop-extension-by-zero-and-arbitrary-base-change]. By the explicit normalization in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], composing this exchange with proper exchange is exactly compact-support exchange. Thus the two constituent unit and counit squares of Step 4 commute. Pasting them, [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (2) says that the resulting square is the square for the composite adjunction with unit and counit as written in Step 4. For the induction, [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] makes compact-support exchange compatible with composition, and [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] makes the right-adjoint pullback identifications compatible with the twist reassociations in Step 5. More explicitly, put $L_i=Rp_{i!}$, $R_i=p_i^*(-)(i)[2i]$, $A_i=Ra_{i+1,!}$ and $B_i=a_{i+1}^*(-)(1)[2]$. Before the twist identification, the induction step has unit $B_i\eta^{p_i}A_i\circ\eta^{a_{i+1}}$ and counit $\epsilon^{p_i}\circ L_i\epsilon^{a_{i+1}}R_i$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Pulling back these displayed composites gives the composites of the pulled-back units and counits by functoriality. Replace each constituent by its primed-base unit or counit using the two constituent base-change squares already proved. The interchange law for natural transformations identifies the resulting composites with $B'_i\eta^{p'_i}A'_i\circ\eta^{a'_{i+1}}$ and $\epsilon^{p'_i}\circ L'_i\epsilon^{a'_{i+1}}R'_i$. The mate-pasting identity just cited identifies their left comparison with compact-support exchange, and twist pullback identifies their right comparison with that for $R_{i+1}$. These are the required unit and counit squares at $i+1$, proving the base-change induction for every $d$. The identity case has identity maps. Fully faithful transport in Step 2 proves the asserted equations on the classical pro-etale categories as well.

source.place: Proof (1), last three sentences: counit, associativity and base-change compatibility

proof.text:
For (2) first work on the ordinary etale categories, writing $G_f$ for the right adjoint of Step 3. The first assertion of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] gives $Du_!\dashv u^*$ on the whole unbounded categories; [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact] identifies $Ru_!$ with this exact sum extension, compatibly with further etale composition. The composition comparison $\alpha_{f,u}:Rf_!Du_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(fu)_!$ of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] therefore gives for every $M,L$ natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,u^*G_fL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Du_!M,G_fL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!Du_!M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R(fu)_!M,L).$$
This exhibits $u^*G_f$ as a right adjoint of $R(fu)_!$. Compare it to $G_{fu}$ by [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. The resulting canonical isomorphism transports by Step 2, whose pullback comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], to exactly $u^*f^!N\cong(fu)^!N$. No boundedness or constructibility condition entered any Hom bijection.

source.place: Proof (2), four Hom groups and the canonical identification (G10)

proof.text:
Write $L_f=Rf_!$, $L_u=Du_!$, $R_f=G_f$, $R_u=u^*$. The composite unit and counit are
$$\eta^{f,u}=R_u\eta^f L_u\circ\eta^u,\qquad \epsilon^{f,u}=\epsilon^f\circ L_f\epsilon^u R_f$$
by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. After identifying $L_fL_u$ with $L_{fu}$ by $\alpha_{f,u}$, let $\theta:u^*G_f\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{fu}$ be the comparison in Step 8. Its defining equation is
$$\epsilon^{fu}\circ L_{fu}\theta=\epsilon^{f,u}\circ\alpha_{f,u}^{-1}(u^*G_f).$$
Thus it preserves the counit, and by adjunction the same equation preserves the unit. For a further separated finite-type etale $v:V\to U$, let $L_v=Dv_!$, $R_v=v^*$. There is a canonical $L_uL_v\cong L_{uv}$: both left adjoints of $v^*u^*=(uv)^*$ are identified by their adjunctions, and the sum-extension comparison of [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact] sends each nested lift summand to its composite lift. Its counit is evaluation on that summand, so it is precisely the counit-preserving left-adjoint comparison. After identifying compact supports by the same node, both parenthesizations of the triple composite adjunction have counit
$$\epsilon^f\circ L_f\epsilon^uR_f\circ L_fL_u\epsilon^vR_uR_f.$$
Indeed the $f,u$-then-$v$ parenthesization substitutes $\epsilon^{f,u}=\epsilon^f\circ L_f\epsilon^uR_f$; the $f$-then-$u,v$ parenthesization substitutes $\epsilon^{u,v}=\epsilon^u\circ L_u\epsilon^vR_u$, and functoriality of $L_f$ gives the same displayed expression. Associativity of $\alpha$ [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] identifies the two left functors with $L_{fuv}$. Therefore the two comparisons of right adjoints preserve the same counit, and are equal by [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. Identity units, counits and $\alpha$ give identity comparisons. If another compact-support functor $L_g$ is composed on the left, both expanded counits are $\epsilon^g\circ L_g\epsilon^fR_g\circ L_gL_f\epsilon^uR_fR_g$; the same associativity and uniqueness prove the requested compatibility with compact-support composition. Finally the pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] respects compositions, so transporting these equations gives the claimed unit, counit, composition and further-localization compatibilities for (G10).

split_report.summary: Made the implicit finite ell-primary coefficient convention and classical unbounded categories explicit; supplied classical adjoint existence, expanded the affine-space induction including d=0, and wrote the unit/counit and localization coherence equations. Two new statement-only lemmas supply the unbounded classical comparison and the quasi-finite exact-support comparison. All other inputs reuse existing nodes. The returned delivery exposed missing chapter/unit records in the then-current side snapshot; the current DAG now contains sec-six-functors-basics and sk-lem-geo-affine-local, and the two new nodes retain those bindings. The route is the standard projective-line/open-extension computation, with no SGA source. Refreshed against the current DAG after the metadata return, filled the current unit realization, and distinguished the changed comparison node’s unbounded inverse-image square from its bounded-below direct-image assertion. Maintainer-reader fix (2026-10-17): the new comparison node is reduced to the unbounded essential-image/counit assertion; full faithfulness and unbounded direct images now cite the existing lem-sfb-unbounded-site-comparison and lem-sfb-unbounded-direct-image-comparison; the standing field is stated as finite or algebraically closed instead of only the algebraic closure of a finite field.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 takes preservation of Noetherianness under finite-type maps, needed for the ordinary etale interfaces; the unit has no separate geometry lemma.
Step 1 needs existence of compactifications for general f and fu; this is the chapter-prescribed Nagata input.
Step 1 takes the standard affine chart of projective space to form the prescribed affine-line compactification.
Step 1 takes properness of the projective-line projection, the proper half of that compactification.
Steps 2, 8 and 9 take the canonical pullback comparison and its composition law for passage between the two sites.
Step 2 needs comparison of etale and pro-etale open extension, a generic site-comparison input missing from this unit.
Steps 2 and 6-9 need unbounded compact-support refinement, composition and base-change maps with their canonical normalization; bounded-below inputs are insufficient.
Steps 2 and 7 need the general categorical equations for mates of pasted squares to identify the canonical exchange maps.
Step 3 needs existence of the ordinary unbounded etale compact-support right adjoint before transporting it; the unit does not supply an existence proof.
Steps 4, 7 and 8 take only exactness and the unbounded etale sum-extension adjunction from its first assertion; G10 is proved here by the Hom calculation.
Steps 4 and 7 take the normalized finite-coefficient ordinary P1 adjunction and its base-change law, exactly the projective-line route prescribed by the unit.
Steps 4, 5 and 7 need canonical pullback of finite Tate lines, powers and shifts, to identify the computed right adjoint.
Steps 4 and 6 need the module-linear inverse-image composition comparison, applied termwise in the induction.
Step 4 needs exactness of constant-module inverse image to use its composition and shift maps on unbounded complexes.
Step 5 needs flatness of the finite Tate lines; their definition alone would not justify computing derived tensor termwise.
Step 5 needs monoidality of derived pullback for the comparison of the two sites; the unit has no replacement for this ringed-topos tool.
Step 7 needs invertibility of the canonical module base-change mate for open extension, applied degreewise.
